How much THC does Limosa have?

article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 70% Indica / 30% Sativa
Genetics: Lemon Miracle × Orange Punch
Breeder: Black Farm Genetix
THC Content: Up to 30%
CBD Content: Low
Terpene Profile: N/A
Primary Flavors: Sweet orange, sour lemon, citrus fruit
Flowering Time (Indoor): 9–10 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: October
Indoor Yield: 600+ g/m²
Outdoor Yield: High
Grow Difficulty: Easy to moderate

Limosa is the kind of cannabis cultivar that announces itself through aroma before potency ever enters the conversation. Developed by Black Farm Genetix as a cross of Lemon Miracle and Orange Punch, this citrus-driven hybrid was selected around an unusually intense combination of sour lemon and ripe orange fragrance, heavy resin production and vigorous plant growth. The breeder considers Limosa one of its signature creations and reports THC potential reaching 30% or higher under favorable conditions, along with a substantial indoor yield exceeding 600 grams per square meter. Black Farm also describes the strain as particularly attractive for extraction because of its combination of abundant trichomes and concentrated aromatic character.

Unlike many modern marijuana varieties that pile dessert sweetness, gas and fruit into the same profile, this cultivar remains firmly focused on citrus. Orange sweetness provides much of the body, while a sharper lemon edge supplies contrast. The effect of that combination is less like generic fruit candy and closer to freshly cut citrus layered with sweet tropical notes. Its potent cannabinoid production and resin-heavy flowers give Limosa appeal beyond flavor alone, making it relevant to flower consumers, home growers and hash or concentrate enthusiasts looking for aromatic starting material.
Genetics and Lineage

The authentic Black Farm Genetix Limosa is Lemon Miracle × Orange Punch. That lineage is published directly by the breeder, which is important because other unrelated cultivars have appeared under the Limosa name. Black Farm lists its version as a 70/30 indica-to-sativa hybrid and identifies it as one of the company’s signature strains.

Lemon Miracle provides much of the sharper citrus and resin-producing character in the equation, while Orange Punch reinforces sweeter orange notes and contributes to the plant’s fruit-centered aromatic identity. Together, the parents produce something more concentrated than a simple lemon-and-orange mixture. The finished cultivar can express sweet citrus peel, sour lemon, tropical fruit and deeper cannabis undertones, giving the aroma enough contrast to remain recognizable after curing.

The importance of Limosa within Black Farm’s program is also visible in the breeder’s later work. The company has incorporated the cultivar into additional crosses, using it as breeding material rather than treating it as a one-off release. That continued use suggests that characteristics such as resin production, plant vigor and citrus expression were valuable enough to preserve in subsequent generations. Black Farm itself calls Limosa a multiple-cup-winning cultivar and one of its favorite creations.
Effects and Experience

Despite its 70% indica classification, Limosa should not automatically be interpreted as a strain that produces immediate couch-lock. At moderate amounts, the experience can begin with a noticeable change in mood and mental atmosphere before heavier physical relaxation develops. Euphoria and a brighter emotional tone may arrive first, while the body gradually feels looser and less tense. That progression can make the weed more versatile than its indica-heavy genetics initially suggest.

Potency changes the character considerably. With breeder-reported THC potential reaching around 30% or higher, Limosa belongs at the powerful end of contemporary cannabis. Experienced consumers may find smaller amounts functional enough for a relaxed afternoon or evening, whereas larger sessions can create substantial body heaviness and mental slowing. For someone with limited THC tolerance, the onset may feel much stronger than the cheerful citrus aroma suggests.

Dose therefore matters more than the indica/sativa percentage alone. Too much high-THC marijuana can produce dry mouth, increased heart rate, dizziness, impaired coordination or anxious thinking in susceptible consumers. Beginning with a modest amount makes it easier to experience the cultivar’s euphoric and relaxing qualities without pushing the high into an uncomfortable range.
Medical Benefits

Limosa has not been studied in controlled clinical trials as a treatment for any specific medical condition. Any medical discussion should therefore distinguish the effects of THC-rich cannabis generally from proven therapeutic effects of this particular strain. Some medical marijuana consumers may nevertheless appreciate a cultivar that combines noticeable mood elevation with increasing physical relaxation, particularly when their goal is to unwind rather than remain highly stimulated.

The experience may make the strain appealing to some people dealing with temporary stress, poor appetite, discomfort or difficulty relaxing in the evening. Strong THC content, however, can be a disadvantage for patients who are sensitive to psychoactive effects. The same amount that one person experiences as calming could cause anxiety, dizziness or excessive sedation in another.

Patients using prescription medication or treating a diagnosed condition should not assume that Limosa’s terpene profile makes it medically predictable. Cannabis flower varies naturally between plants and harvests, and cannabinoid concentrations can differ even within the same genetic line. Package-specific laboratory testing is therefore more useful than relying on a single universal THC number.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Citrus is not simply a background accent with Limosa; it defines the strain. Black Farm Genetix describes the aromatic profile specifically around oranges and sour lemons, reflecting the contribution of both parent lines. Fresh flower can carry an almost juicy quality, beginning with sweet orange before moving toward sharper lemon peel and acidic citrus. The contrast between sweetness and sourness prevents the aroma from becoming flat.

Breaking apart a well-cured bud tends to expose additional depth. Behind the bright fruit can be mild earthy, herbal or oily nuances, particularly in resin-heavy phenotypes. Individual growers have also described selected plants from the line as producing creamy lemon-curd aromas with a faint engine-oil quality, illustrating how different phenotypes can emphasize different parts of the genetic profile.

The flavor follows a similar pattern when the flower is properly dried and cured. Sweet orange appears early, sour lemon becomes more obvious through the middle, and the finish can leave a lingering citrus rind quality. Consumers who specifically seek lemon- or orange-centered weed are likely to find the profile considerably more focused than strains where citrus merely sits beneath dominant gas or dessert notes.
Growing Information

Black Farm provides unusually specific cultivation information for Limosa. The breeder lists a flowering period of approximately nine to ten weeks indoors, an indoor production potential above 600 grams per square meter and an outdoor harvest window in October. It can be cultivated indoors or outdoors and is sold in feminized form. Black Farm describes the plant as robust, vigorous and notably tall, with extensive trichome coverage and high cannabinoid production.

Height management may therefore deserve attention indoors. Training early in vegetative growth can help control vertical stretch and distribute productive branches more evenly across the canopy. Its vigorous structure gives growers room to shape the plant, while good airflow becomes increasingly important as flowers gain density and resin late in bloom. The breeder considers Limosa easy to grow, making it more approachable than many high-potency specialty cultivars.

Resin production is one of the cultivar’s most interesting horticultural traits. Black Farm specifically highlights it as a favorite among extractors and reports fresh-frozen returns above 5%. Growers interested in hash or rosin may therefore find Limosa especially attractive. Careful drying remains important for flower production because excessive heat or rapid moisture loss can mute the volatile compounds responsible for its defining lemon-and-orange aroma.
FAQ
What is the Limosa strain?

Limosa is an indica-dominant hybrid bred by Black Farm Genetix. The breeder created it by crossing Lemon Miracle with Orange Punch and classifies the resulting cultivar as approximately 70% indica and 30% sativa.
What are the genetics of Limosa?
The verified genetics are Lemon Miracle × Orange Punch. Other cannabis cultivars have appeared under the same Limosa name, so checking the breeder is important when identifying the strain.
How much THC does Limosa have?

Black Farm Genetix states that its Limosa can reach THC levels around 30% or higher. Actual potency depends on phenotype, cultivation conditions, harvest maturity and laboratory testing, so individual batches may be lower.
What does Limosa taste like?
Sweet orange and sour lemon dominate the profile, accompanied by broader citrus and tropical fruit qualities. Some individual phenotypes may also develop creamy, earthy or slightly oily undertones.
Is Limosa easy to grow?

Black Farm Genetix describes Limosa as very easy to cultivate and suitable for both indoor and outdoor environments. The plant is vigorous and can become tall, with an indoor flowering period of roughly nine to ten weeks and potentially high yields.
Final Thoughts on Limosa

Limosa succeeds because it has a clearly defined purpose. Black Farm Genetix did not create a hybrid that simply checks the usual boxes of high THC, sweetness and heavy resin; the cultivar revolves around a concentrated citrus identity supported by serious production potential. Lemon Miracle and Orange Punch combine into flower that can move from sweet orange toward sour lemon while retaining the potency expected from modern marijuana genetics.

Its cultivation characteristics make the strain equally noteworthy. A nine-to-ten-week flowering cycle, breeder-reported indoor yields above 600 g/m² and abundant trichome production give growers several reasons to consider it beyond flavor alone. For consumers, Limosa offers potent hybrid effects wrapped in one of the more direct citrus profiles in contemporary cannabis. For cultivators and extract makers, its vigorous structure and resin output explain why Black Farm continues to regard the cultivar as a cornerstone of its breeding program.
